source_assets.text:
Othello
by William Shakespeare

About the play

Othello is a tragedy by William Shakespeare, written around 1603. It tells the story of Othello, a Black African general who leads the army of Venice. Othello is respected and powerful, but in Venice he is also an outsider. One of his own officers, Iago, secretly hates him. Over the course of the play, Iago sets out to destroy Othello using nothing but lies.

The opening scene: Act 1, Scene 1

The play begins in the middle of the night, on a street in Venice. We meet two characters, Roderigo and Iago. They are arguing about shocking news: Othello has just secretly married Desdemona, the daughter of a powerful senator, Brabantio.

Roderigo wanted to marry Desdemona himself, and he has been paying Iago to help him. Iago has his own reason to be angry: Othello has made a man called Cassio his lieutenant instead of him. By the end of the scene, Iago has woken Brabantio with the news, and slipped away into the dark.

source_assets.text:
RODERIGO
Tush, never tell me! I take it much unkindly
That thou, Iago, who hast had my purse
As if the strings were thine, shouldst know of this.
IAGO
'Sblood, but you'll not hear me!
If ever I did dream of such a matter,
Abhor me.
RODERIGO
Thou toldst me thou didst hold him in thy hate.
IAGO
Despise me
If I do not. Three great ones of the city,
In personal suit to make me his lieutenant,
Off-capped to him; and, by the faith of man,
I know my price, I am worth no worse a place.

[Iago explains that Othello turned the great men down, saying he had already chosen his officer.]
IAGO
And what was he?
Forsooth, a great arithmetician,
One Michael Cassio, a Florentine,
...That never set a squadron in the field...
And I, of whom his eyes had seen the proof
At Rhodes, at Cyprus, and on other grounds
Christened and heathen, must be beleed and calmed
By debitor and creditor.
...He, in good time, must his lieutenant be,
And I, God bless the mark, his Moorship's ancient.
...Preferment goes by letter and affection,
And not by old gradation, where each second
Stood heir to th' first. Now, sir, be judge yourself
Whether I in any just term am affined
To love the Moor.
source_assets.rights: Authored source credits abridged Folger Shakespeare text CC BY-NC 3.0; attribution retained; authored instructional additions have no separate rights determination.

source_assets.text:
RODERIGO
I would not follow him, then.
IAGO
O, sir, content you.
I follow him to serve my turn upon him.
We cannot all be masters, nor all masters
Cannot be truly followed. (lines 45–47)
...It is as sure as you are Roderigo,
Were I the Moor I would not be Iago.
In following him, I follow but myself.
Heaven is my judge, not I for love and duty,
But seeming so for my peculiar end.
For when my outward action doth demonstrate
The native act and figure of my heart
In complement extern, 'tis not long after
But I will wear my heart upon my sleeve
For daws to peck at. I am not what I am.

source_assets.text:
RODERIGO
What a full fortune does the thick-lips owe
If he can carry 't thus!
IAGO
Call up her father.
Rouse him. Make after him, poison his delight...
[They go to Brabantio's house.]
IAGO
Awake! What ho, Brabantio! Thieves, thieves!
Look to your house, your daughter, and your bags!
Thieves, thieves!
[Hidden in the dark, Iago shouts crude, racist insults about Othello and Desdemona. Brabantio is horrified. Before he can be seen, Iago tells Roderigo he must leave.]

source_assets.text:
IAGO
Though I do hate him as I do hell pains,
Yet, for necessity of present life,
I must show out a flag and sign of love—
Which is indeed but sign. (lines 171–174)
[Iago leaves. Brabantio gathers his men to find Othello.]

source_assets.text:
At the beginning of the play, Shakespeare exposes Iago as deceitful and disloyal to Othello.
"I answer the Learning Question first, with two words from my web."

This is evident in the quote "I follow him to serve my turn upon him."
"I choose a short quote that proves my point."

The verb "follow" means to obey a leader, demonstrating that on the outside Iago looks like a loyal soldier.
"Now one word. 'Follow' sounds loyal: that's the façade."

Also, the verb "serve" usually means to work for someone, but "serve my turn" means to use them for your own benefit, demonstrating that Iago plans to betray Othello.
"The second word shows what's behind the façade."

Therefore, Iago is clearly exposed to be a Machiavellian villain: his loyalty is only a pretense and a façade.
"I answer the Learning Question again, more strongly."

known_constraints: Create exactly 14 newly authored response checks in blueprint order using question-set 0.1 kinds: 2 classify, 3 evidence_select, 3 open_check, 1 open_prompt, 5 reading_mcq.
The supplied aim and content targets come from an existing authored lesson. Phase order, pairing and check placement are proposals for this prototype, not official course approval.

Do not reproduce old authored questions, choices, answer keys, marker rubrics or close prompts. No such question data is in this request. The clearly marked worked model is instruction and must not count as an independent check.

Use exact supplied dialogue wording, punctuation, omissions, speaker labels and stage directions. Attribute quotations to the actual speaker. Do not silently replace the abridgement with another edition or unabridged lines.
Do not treat Iago's accusations about Cassio as neutral narrator-established facts or assume that his claim to Roderigo proves he had known about the secret marriage.
No film-dependent, performance-dependent, audio-dependent or outside-scene knowledge questions: exact media assets are not supplied.
Each response check asks one assessable operation. Q14 is a whole paragraph performance; its scaffolding does not turn it into five independent checks.

Each keyed claim and open rubric must be supported by the supplied scene; allow other defensible interpretations. Evidence selections must use complete meaningful units in source order and offer the strongest evidence.
Keep the worked model on a different page from response checks. Do not display source interpretations, hints or answer feedback beside a check before its first response.

Later checks share targets and prior teaching. Independent means the learner gives a response without an answer hint; this is not fourteen statistically independent measurements or evidence of unaided mastery.
No measured learner difficulty, ZPD match, instructional effectiveness, academic approval or evaluator qualification is established by this input.
Return a question-set plus a generated lesson-context where every item.pointer resolves to its actual native unit. Preserve target/source/phase placement metadata for review.
